newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends mostly lower with cash, gas.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends mostly lower with cash, gas.

text.p: Most NYMEX electricity futures settled lower Friday with falling spot cash prices and natural gas futures in a thin session which Palo Verde (PV) volume outpacted California-Oregon Border (COB).
"It was just a very thin market. It looks directionless right now," said an East Coast paper broker.
Concerns over rising hydroelectric output in the Northwest continued to underpin the psychology of many players, market sources noted.
March COB settled down 13 cents at $10.90 a megawatt hour (MWh) after bouncing in 10 cent range.
April COB finished down five cents at $10.05. Other active COB contracts also ended five cents lower.
March PV settled up two cents at $13.30 after traded between $12.85 and $13.30.
April PV finished up 15 cents at $12.25. Other active PV months ended flat to 25 cents lower.
In over-the-counter activity after the close, March COB was discussed at $10.75-11.00 and March PV $13.20-13.30. Third-quarter 1997 COB was talked at $16.30-16.50 and third-quarter PV $22.25-22.30.
Firm, peak daily COB and PV power prices for Monday fell 50 cents to $1.50 from Thursday's level.
NYMEX March natgas futures settled down 17.9 cents at $2.182 per million British thermal units.
Forecasts called for the Pacific Northwest to see temperatures from two to five degrees Fahrenheit below normal for the next several days, with some moisture in the western portions of the region.
Longer-term forecasts called for below and much below temperatures through most of the Northwest from Feb 11 to 15.
In the Southwest, forecasts called for temperatures to be three to six degrees below normal into Saturday, with some scattered light precipitation over the north and western sections.
The Southwest was expected to see near normal temperatures from Feb 11 to 15, with the exception of Arizona which was called to have above-normal temperatures.
A 1,100 megawatt (MW) pumped storage hydroelectric plant near Fresno, Calif., was shut last Saturday for mechanical repairs, and could stay down for up to two weeks.

The 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant at Richland, Wash., was operating at 67 percent of capacity as of early Friday but will reduce power to 25 pct of capacity due to ongoing problems with an adjustble speed drive.
NYMEX estimated 73 COB and 265 PV contracts were sold, compared with Thursday's sales of 392 COB and 168 PV.
